lines.text: Bob flips seven coins, and his friend Ann flips five. Who gets more heads?
lines.caption: Bob flips seven coins, and his friend Ann flips five. Who gets more heads?

lines.text: Bob has two extra coins, so he should usually win. But how often, exactly?
lines.caption: Bob has two extra coins, so he should usually win. But how often, exactly?

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Today, one little flip turns a race into a single count.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Today, one little flip turns a race into a single count.

lines.text: Here's the question. Our friend Ann flips five fair coins, and Bob flips seven fair coins.
lines.caption: Here's the question. Our friend Ann flips five fair coins, and Bob flips seven fair coins.

lines.text: What is the probability that Bob gets more heads than Ann?
lines.caption: What is the probability that Bob gets more heads than Ann?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: So what do we know? Every coin is fair: heads and tails are equally likely.
lines.caption: So what do we know? Every coin is fair: heads and tails are equally likely.

lines.text: We want Bob's heads to be MORE than Ann's heads. A tie does not count.
lines.caption: We want Bob's heads to be MORE than Ann's heads. A tie does not count.

lines.text: Comparing two piles of coins is tricky. Let's see if we can turn it into ONE count.
lines.caption: Comparing two piles of coins is tricky. Let's see if we can turn it into ONE count.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back!
lines.caption: Welcome back!

lines.text: Look at Ann's coins. Her heads are five minus her tails, like three heads and two tails.
lines.caption: Look at Ann's coins. Her heads are five minus her tails, like three heads and two tails.

lines.text: So Bob wins when his heads beat five minus Ann's tails.
lines.caption: So Bob wins when his heads beat five minus Ann's tails.

lines.text: Move Ann's tails across: Bob's heads plus Ann's tails is more than five, so at least six.
lines.caption: Move Ann's tails across: Bob's heads plus Ann's tails is more than five, so at least six.

lines.text: Now flip all of Ann's coins over. Her tails turn into heads.
lines.caption: Now flip all of Ann's coins over. Her tails turn into heads.

lines.text: Flipped fair coins are still fair coins, so every chance stays the same.
lines.caption: Flipped fair coins are still fair coins, so every chance stays the same.

lines.text: So Bob wins exactly when twelve fair coins show at least six heads.
lines.caption: So Bob wins exactly when twelve fair coins show at least six heads.

lines.text: Twelve coins can land two to the twelfth ways. That's four thousand ninety-six.
lines.caption: Twelve coins can land two to the twelfth ways. That's four thousand ninety-six.

lines.text: Sort them into three piles: fewer than six heads, exactly six, and more than six.
lines.caption: Sort them into three piles: fewer than six heads, exactly six, and more than six.

lines.text: The outer piles are mirror images. Swap every head and tail, and one turns into the other.
lines.caption: The outer piles are mirror images. Swap every head and tail, and one turns into the other.

lines.text: The middle pile is twelve choose six: pick which six coins show heads.
lines.caption: The middle pile is twelve choose six: pick which six coins show heads.

lines.text: Multiply twelve down to seven, then divide by six down to one. That's nine hundred twenty-four.
lines.caption: Multiply twelve down to seven, then divide by six down to one. That's nine hundred twenty-four.

lines.text: Four thousand ninety-six minus nine hundred twenty-four is three thousand one hundred seventy-two.
lines.caption: Four thousand ninety-six minus nine hundred twenty-four is three thousand one hundred seventy-two.

lines.text: The two outer piles share that evenly: one thousand five hundred eighty-six each.
lines.caption: The two outer piles share that evenly: one thousand five hundred eighty-six each.

lines.text: At least six heads means the middle pile plus the top pile.
lines.caption: At least six heads means the middle pile plus the top pile.

lines.text: Nine hundred twenty-four plus one thousand five hundred eighty-six is two thousand five hundred ten.
lines.caption: Nine hundred twenty-four plus one thousand five hundred eighty-six is two thousand five hundred ten.

lines.text: So the chance is two thousand five hundred ten over four thousand ninety-six.
lines.caption: So the chance is two thousand five hundred ten over four thousand ninety-six.

lines.text: Divide both by two: one thousand two hundred fifty-five over two thousand forty-eight. That's Choice D!
lines.caption: Divide both by two: one thousand two hundred fifty-five over two thousand forty-eight. That's Choice D!

scenes.chapter: Solution 2: fair game plus a tiebreak

lines.text: Here's another way. Hide one of Bob's coins for now: six coins against five.
lines.caption: Here's another way. Hide one of Bob's coins for now: six coins against five.

lines.text: Now Bob has more heads than Ann, or more tails than Ann. Exactly one of the two!
lines.caption: Now Bob has more heads than Ann, or more tails than Ann. Exactly one of the two!

lines.text: More of neither, and he'd have five coins at most. More of both, and he'd need seven.
lines.caption: More of neither, and he'd have five coins at most. More of both, and he'd need seven.

lines.text: Heads and tails are equally likely, so Bob wins this six-coin game exactly half the time.
lines.caption: Heads and tails are equally likely, so Bob wins this six-coin game exactly half the time.

lines.text: Now bring back coin seven. It only matters when Bob's six coins tie with Ann.
lines.caption: Now bring back coin seven. It only matters when Bob's six coins tie with Ann.

lines.text: To find a tie, flip Ann's coins again. A tie means exactly five heads among eleven coins.
lines.caption: To find a tie, flip Ann's coins again. A tie means exactly five heads among eleven coins.

lines.text: Eleven choose five is four hundred sixty-two, out of two to the eleventh, two thousand forty-eight.
lines.caption: Eleven choose five is four hundred sixty-two, out of two to the eleventh, two thousand forty-eight.

lines.text: Coin seven lands heads on half of those ties: two hundred thirty-one more wins.
lines.caption: Coin seven lands heads on half of those ties: two hundred thirty-one more wins.

lines.text: One half is one thousand twenty-four over two thousand forty-eight. Add two hundred thirty-one.
lines.caption: One half is one thousand twenty-four over two thousand forty-eight. Add two hundred thirty-one.

lines.text: One thousand two hundred fifty-five over two thousand forty-eight. Same answer!
lines.caption: One thousand two hundred fifty-five over two thousand forty-eight. Same answer!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? With just one extra coin, it gives one half right away.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? With just one extra coin, it gives one half right away.

lines.text: Now the traps! First, let's write all five choices over two thousand forty-eight.
lines.caption: Now the traps! First, let's write all five choices over two thousand forty-eight.

lines.text: Choice A is the top pile alone. That's what you'd get if exactly six heads didn't count.
lines.caption: Choice A is the top pile alone. That's what you'd get if exactly six heads didn't count.

lines.text: Choice B, one half, is right for six coins against five. Bob's seventh coin adds the tiebreak wins.
lines.caption: Choice B, one half, is right for six coins against five. Bob's seventh coin adds the tiebreak wins.

lines.text: Choice E adds the pile with exactly five heads. That's what you'd get if a tie counted as a win.
lines.caption: Choice E adds the pile with exactly five heads. That's what you'd get if a tie counted as a win.

lines.text: Choice C, five hundred seventy-five over one thousand twenty-four, is sneakier.
lines.caption: Choice C, five hundred seventy-five over one thousand twenty-four, is sneakier.

lines.text: That's what you'd get if Bob's first five coins raced Ann's, and his two spares only broke ties.
lines.caption: That's what you'd get if Bob's first five coins raced Ann's, and his two spares only broke ties.

lines.text: But Bob can also come back from one behind, when both spares land heads!
lines.caption: But Bob can also come back from one behind, when both spares land heads!

lines.text: So here's a great habit: always ask if a tie counts. MORE than, or at least?
lines.caption: So here's a great habit: always ask if a tie counts. MORE than, or at least?

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Now our friend Ann flips three fair coins, and Bob flips five.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Now our friend Ann flips three fair coins, and Bob flips five.

lines.text: What is the probability that Bob gets more heads than Ann?
lines.caption: What is the probability that Bob gets more heads than Ann?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. Flip Ann's three coins over. Bob needs at least four heads among eight coins.
lines.caption: Let's check. Flip Ann's three coins over. Bob needs at least four heads among eight coins.

lines.text: Eight coins land two to the eighth ways: two hundred fifty-six. Eight choose four is seventy.
lines.caption: Eight coins land two to the eighth ways: two hundred fifty-six. Eight choose four is seventy.

lines.text: The rest, two hundred fifty-six minus seventy, is one hundred eighty-six: ninety-three each.
lines.caption: The rest, two hundred fifty-six minus seventy, is one hundred eighty-six: ninety-three each.

lines.text: At least four heads: seventy plus ninety-three is one hundred sixty-three.
lines.caption: At least four heads: seventy plus ninety-three is one hundred sixty-three.

lines.text: The answer is one hundred sixty-three over two hundred fifty-six. If you got it, amazing work!
lines.caption: The answer is one hundred sixty-three over two hundred fifty-six. If you got it, amazing work!

lines.text: Flip one player's coins over. Fair coins stay fair, so the chances don't change.
lines.caption: Flip one player's coins over. Fair coins stay fair, so the chances don't change.

lines.text: Then a race for more heads becomes one count, for one big pile of coins.
lines.caption: Then a race for more heads becomes one count, for one big pile of coins.
